To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) it is difficult to identify a single model structure that performs best for all catchments; (ii) the performance of different model structures varies widely among catchments; (iii) the ranking of model structures is not clearly related to catchment characteristics; and (iv) the selection of model structures for lumped conceptual models should not be based on a prior assessment of model performance, but should be done based on a posteriori model comparisons.

(i) for some catchments, multiple model structures perform equally well; and (ii), for the spatial scales and model structures considered in this study, it is difficult (or even impossible) to base model selection on prior information.

the relative performance of a set (12 in this case) of lumped conceptual hydrological models is highly dependent on the catchment to which these models were applied, and that there is no simple rule that allows to identify the best model structure for a given catchment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can the performance of a model be predicted by a priori knowledge about the model structure and catchment characteristics?
the identification of model structures that can be considered to be appropriate for the catchments considered in this study.
the question whether it is possible, based on the characteristics of the catchment, to select a model structure that performs well in that catchment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a given model structure is highly dependent on the catchment in which it is applied.
it is not possible to identify the single best model for a given catchment.
catchment classification is possible, but only by means of multiple model structures, and not by means of a single model structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selection of a model structure for a given application is a trade-off between model performance, data availability, and model complexity.
it is possible to find a best structure for each catchment.

it is possible to select the best model for a particular catchment by comparing the model performance for a set of models, but that it is difficult to select a model based on prior information on the catchment characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of a model structure is not trivial and that a priori assessment is not sufficient to ensure that a selected model structure will perform well.
model selection is a complex process and that it cannot be based on a single set of criteria.
it is not possible to identify a best model for all catchments, but rather that the best model depends on the catchment to which it is applied.
